About SCOME

What is
SCOME?

The Standing Committee on Medical Education (SCOME) is one of the oldest Standing Committees in IFMSA — established in 1951.

EKSUMSA SCOME is the local chapter at Ekiti State University, Ado-Ekiti — elevating medical education quality through research, advocacy, and peer learning.

IFMSA AffiliateNiMSA MemberAdo-Ekiti, NigeriaEst. 1951
SCOME
Our Foundation

Vision &
Mission

Vision Statement

Medical students are meaningfully engaged within their Medical Education Systems — representing student voice on all levels to create quality Medical Education worldwide.

Mission Statement

SCOME creates a shared environment where medical students contribute, reflect and work on Medical Education through education, research, capacity development, youth engagement and advocacy.

Strategic Focus

Pillars of
SCOME

01
Medical Education Quality
Advocacy for evidence-based teaching and learning standards at all levels.
02
Research & Innovation
Driving student-led medical education research and evidence-based practice.
03
Capacity Development
Building leadership and clinical competencies through structured programs.
04
Advocacy & Feedback
Representing student interests in medical education policy and reform.
05
Public Health Engagement
Awareness campaigns, outreach, and community health education.

Featured Write-up

Research
Spotlight.

TB
World TB Day 2026

Global Tuberculosis Paradigms: Epidemiological Shifts, Therapeutic Innovations & Emerging Research Frontiers

A comprehensive analysis of where TB control stands in 2026 — from post-pandemic recovery and ultra-short drug regimens to AI diagnostics and the socioeconomic inequities driving transmission in high-burden regions including Nigeria.

10.7M
Global cases (2024)
1.23M
Deaths recorded
18
Vaccine trials
Key Findings
  • Asymptomatic TB causes 25–51% of all transmission
  • New 4-month DS-TB regimen now conditionally recommended
  • BPaLM 6-month replaces injections for MDR/RR-TB
  • M72/AS01E vaccine showed 50% efficacy in Phase IIb
  • AI models trained on 32,000 Mtb genomes identifying targets
  • 50% of TB households face catastrophic financial costs
Written by
Director of Academics & Research
EKSUMSA SCOME · March 2026

Department of Physiology · EKSU · March 24, 2026
SCOME team after the campus activation
Education

Know TB.

01 · What is TB
Tuberculosis Basics
Chronic disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis
Primarily targets the lungs (pulmonary TB)
Can spread to bones, brain, kidneys
Preventable. Curable. Still killing millions.
01
02 · Symptoms
Red Flags
Persistent cough >2 weeks — the hallmark
Night sweats — profuse sweating during sleep
Unexplained progressive weight loss
Low-grade fever, fatigue, haemoptysis
02
03 · Prevention
Stay Safe
BCG vaccination — protects neonates
Good ventilation in homes and schools
Respiratory hygiene — cover when coughing
Early screening for at-risk individuals
03
04 · Treatment
Treatment Protocol
6-month four-drug therapy: Isoniazid, Rifampicin, Pyrazinamide, Ethambutol
Incomplete treatment creates MDR/XDR-TB
DOTS ensures full treatment adherence
04
05 · Myths Busted
Facts vs Myths
"TB cannot be cured" — FALSE. Curable with treatment
"TB is a disease of the past" — FALSE. 10.7M in 2024
"TB is hereditary" — FALSE. Bacterial disease
05
06 · Transmission
How TB Spreads
Airborne — cough, sneeze, speech droplets
Droplet nuclei remain infectious for hours
NOT spread by handshakes or food sharing
06

Clinical Education

Clinical Case
Scenarios.

CASE 01Pulmonary TB
Classic Pulmonary TB

A 28-year-old man presents with chronic cough, low-grade fever, night sweats, progressive weight loss. Recently coughing blood. Lives in a crowded apartment.

Diagnosis
Active pulmonary TB — Mycobacterium tuberculosis
Key Clue
Cough + haemoptysis + constitutional symptoms
SCOME EKSUMSA · Educational Case
CASE 02Latent TB
Latent TB — Asymptomatic

A 22-year-old medical student undergoes routine screening. Reports no symptoms. Mantoux (TST) positive. Chest X-ray completely normal.

Diagnosis
Latent TB — bacteria present but contained; not infectious
Key Clue
Positive TST + no symptoms + normal CXR
SCOME EKSUMSA · Educational Case
CASE 03Extrapulmonary
TB Meningitis

A 5-year-old child presents with fever, neck stiffness, altered consciousness. Symptoms developed gradually over 2 weeks.

Diagnosis
Extrapulmonary TB — TB Meningitis
Key Clue
Subacute onset — atypical of bacterial meningitis
SCOME EKSUMSA · Educational Case
CASE 04Extrapulmonary
TB Pericarditis

A 50-year-old man presents with chest pain, shortness of breath, bilateral leg swelling. Muffled heart sounds on examination.

Diagnosis
Extrapulmonary TB — TB Pericarditis with effusion
Key Clue
Muffled sounds + raised JVP + hypotension = Beck's Triad
SCOME EKSUMSA · Educational Case
